stem: In which child are oral corticosteroids most clearly indicated?

options.text: A child with cough but no wheeze
A child with acute asthma not adequately responding to inhaled salbutamol
A preschool child with mild viral wheeze that has fully settled
A child with uncomplicated viral upper respiratory symptoms

explanation: Systemic corticosteroids are indicated for acute asthma exacerbations when symptoms are more than mild or not responding adequately to bronchodilator therapy. They are not routinely used for bronchiolitis or uncomplicated viral cough.
